text: Approach: start from economically motivated families rather than blind search, then insist on parameter-neighbourhood robustness before trusting any train SR. Batch 1 mapped raw families: short horizon returns ret(3/5/10) carry SR near -1.0 to -1.2, ma(5) and minr(20) and maxr(20) all point the same way, so the dominant effect in this panel is cross sectional short term reversal. Longer horizon momentum ret(120/250) shows positive rank IC but negative portfolio SR, a magnitude versus rank divergence I distrust, so I set momentum aside. Idiosyncratic skewness is a genuine second effect: neg(skew(20)) and neg(skew(60)) agree in both SR and IC. Two normalizations each gave a large and consistent lift: ts_z of the raw feature over 60 to 120 days, which removes each assets own drift and scale, and dividing by trailing vol, which caps risk contribution from high vol names. Both lifted SR and IC together, which argues they are real rather than variance artifacts. Robustness evidence: div(neg(ts_z(ret(5),120)), std(X)) returns 1.89 to 1.95 for X in 5 20 40 60 120, and div(neg(ts_z(minr(10),120)), std(X)) returns 1.97 to 2.04 over the same range. Flat plateaus over parameters, not isolated spikes. Decay test confirms the mechanism: delaying the reversal input by 3 days drops SR to 0.48 and by 5 days to 0.00, exactly the fast decay a liquidity provision reversal should show. Selection discipline: I am deliberately not chasing the single highest train SR. With hundreds of expressions the max is upward biased, so I will report signals that sit on wide parameter plateaus, have SR and IC agreeing in sign, and rest on a documented economic mechanism.

text: Final selection logic. Three economically distinct effects survive scrutiny in this panel. One, short horizon cross sectional reversal at 3 to 5 days, the classic liquidity provision premium. Two, oversold proximity, the ts z score of price distance above its rolling 10 to 15 day low, which is the same reversal economics measured path dependently rather than point to point. Three, the idiosyncratic skewness anomaly, long low skew and short high skew, the lottery preference premium. Everything else failed. Long horizon momentum showed positive rank IC but negative portfolio SR, a sign conflict I treat as disqualifying. Kurtosis, beta, correlation to the panel, vol spike ratios and absolute return amplitude all produced near zero SR. Two normalizations do the heavy lifting and both are mechanical rather than fitted. ts z over 60 to 120 days removes each assets own drift and scale before ranking, and dividing by trailing vol equalizes risk contribution.
